name: Insurance
description: Insurance UI UX design for quote, policy and claims products: plain-language forms, customer portals and admin tools that make cover easier to buy and use.
image_alt: Advisor reviewing an insurance form with a client, insurance industry
overview:
Insurance asks people to make important decisions with words they rarely use. Long forms, unclear terms and slow claims leave customers unsure what they are paying for. My job is to make cover easy to understand: plain language, short steps and clear status at every stage.

I work with founders and product teams on web and mobile products, from the first prototype to a design system engineers can build from directly. For insurance, that means designing quotes, policies and claims around real customers, with compliance and disclosures planned into the flow from day one.

challenges.title: Long, complex forms
challenges.text: Quote and claim forms ask for a lot of detail, and people give up when they lose track.

challenges.title: Jargon and fine print
challenges.text: Terms such as excess, exclusions and premiums need plain explanations at the right moment.

challenges.title: Claims anxiety
challenges.text: People claim at stressful times and need to know exactly what happens next.

challenges.title: Regulatory disclosures
challenges.text: Required wording and consent have to be clear without burying the main task.

faqs.question: How do you make long insurance forms easier to complete?
faqs.answer: I ask only what is needed at each step, group questions logically and show progress. Save-and-return and clear help text stop people losing work or guessing.

faqs.question: How do you handle compliance and required wording?
faqs.answer: I review the required disclosures and consent with your team early, then design them into the flow so they are clear without blocking the main task.

faqs.question: Can you design claims journeys?
faqs.answer: Yes. I design guided claim forms, document and photo upload, and status tracking, so customers always know what happens next.

faqs.question: Can you work with our existing design system?
faqs.answer: Yes. I can extend and clean up an existing system, or create one from scratch with tokens and components that match your codebase.

faqs.question: How do we start?
faqs.answer: Send me a short brief through the contact page. We will have a call about your product, users and timeline, and I will come back with a plan and quote.
